blocks.text: Separate durable server facts from transient interaction state and optimistic overlays. Row order is a versioned server fact. A card contains display metadata and references progress by title identity. Focus, visible range, and pending commands are client state. Keeping these layers separate lets a failed command disappear without reconstructing the server snapshot and lets a progress delta update one entity without replacing the row.

blocks.title: Ownership and merge policy
rows: Accept only a newer complete revision or a valid delta based on the current revision.
Merge independently so a late row response cannot lower fresh progress.
Overlay the base row; clear on success, conflict, or terminal error.
Keep identity, then derive the nearest valid position after row changes.
Deduplicate by candidate URL and evict by measured memory policy.
Do not switch the visible variant midway through one page session.

blocks.text: The visible title IDs are derived from the authoritative row order minus sending removals. Progress percentage is clamped for display but the raw seconds and revision remain available for resume behavior and diagnostics. Artwork candidates are selected from rendered size, pixel density, format support, and network policy; the selected URL is not duplicated into every view object. A card is considered interactive when its title identity and destination are valid, even if artwork has failed.

blocks.title: Data invariants
items: One title identity maps to one title entity within the active profile scope.
Progress never moves backward solely because an older response arrived later.
A pending command never overwrites the authoritative row revision.
Focus is stored by identity and never by a fragile array index alone.
Large image bytes and decoded bitmaps are not placed in application state.
Profile, locale, maturity permissions, and experiment assignment participate in cache isolation.
Telemetry excludes title names and personal viewing details unless an approved measurement contract explicitly requires them.

blocks.title: Why normalization helps here
blocks.text: Normalization is justified by independent progress deltas, cross-row title reuse, and targeted subscriptions. If a smaller product has one static row and no deltas, a query result plus local view state can be simpler.
